subject: Intersync partner: technical qualification & runbook
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Moreno <alex@intersync.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intersync technical qualification kickoff

Alex —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Per our conversation, we'd like to run a short technical qualification focused on latency guarantees, deployment modes (hosted vs. private), and the integration points for token-level tracing. Goal is to validate the reference architecture so we can move to a pilot.

Proposed next steps:
- Your architecture diagram and a suggested test matrix (latency/throughput/security).
- Red team / compliance checklist items (SOC2-related flows).
- Mutually agreed runbook for provisioning test resources (RDW will run a 2-week smoke + load test).

Can you share the architecture artifact and a first-pass matrix by EOD Tuesday? I’ll loop in Marissa and Karthik to cover solution QA and infra.

Sergio
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai

--
Attachments: none
From: Alex Moreno <alex@intersync.io>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 11:05:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Intersync technical qualification kickoff

Sergio —

Nice to kick this off. Attached is our first-pass reference diagram and an initial test matrix. High level notes:
- We support both hosted (multi-tenant with customer namespace isolation) and private (VPC peering or appliance) deployments.
- For token-level tracing we can emit structured events to your tracing endpoint (configurable via webhook/OTLP).
- We included a proposed set of baseline SLAs (p95 latency targets per model family) in the matrix.

I’ve added Priya (Consultify) who will be our integration lead for the pilot. She’ll coordinate SSO and infra access.

Attachments:
- intersync_arch_diagram_v1.pdf (PDF)
- intersync_test_matrix.xlsx (Excel)

Thanks,
Alex
Principal Solutions Architect, Intersync Labs
alex@intersync.io

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Intersync technical qualification kickoff

Marissa / Karthik —

Forwarding Intersync's artifacts (attached by Alex). Quick asks from our side before we accept the pilot:
1) Can SDM/QA sign off on the test matrix items? Pay particular attention to the p95/p99 SLA rows and the note about KV cache persistence behavior under warm restarts.
2) Security — verify the SSO/SCIM flow is compatible with our IdP patterns and confirm what logs Intersync exposes for audit.
3) Ops — what does their private deployment look like for VPC peering? Do we need a VPN appliance?

I propose a 40-minute architecture gate call on Wednesday 10:00-10:40 PT to agree scope and acceptance criteria. Can you confirm availability?

Sergio

Attachments: intersync_arch_diagram_v1.pdf, intersync_test_matrix.xlsx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Moreno <alex@intersync.io>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 10:22:45 -0700
Subject: Re: FW: Intersync technical qualification kickoff

Sergio —

Thanks for the forward. Quick read-through of the test matrix attached; notes below (high level):

- Latency/Throughput:
  - Add p50, p95, p99 rows for cold vs warm cache (they only have p95/p99 now).
  - Include longer sequence lengths in the load plan (1k tokens) to validate KV cache scaling.

- Stability:
  - Add a planned node-restart during the load window to observe KV persistence and fallback behavior.

- Security / Audit:
  - We need confirmation that trace payloads redact PII before forwarding (sample payload format).
  - Request for SOC2 evidence: uptime reports + access-control policy doc.

- Private deployment:
  - If they require a VPN appliance we need the model of device and throughput estimates; if only VPC peering, we need CIDR and routing details.

I can take the lead on the architecture gate call; Wed 10:00 PT works for me. Karthik — can you confirm you can cover the runbook/ops acceptance?

Marissa
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Moreno <alex@intersync.io>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Kapoor <priya.kapoor@consultify.com>
Date: Thu, 13 May 2026 14:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FW: Intersync technical qualification kickoff

Marissa / Sergio —

Thanks for the notes — really helpful. Quick responses inline:
- p50/p95/p99: we’ll add cold vs warm cache split and extend to 1k token sequences.
- Node restart: we can schedule a controlled restart during the test window and capture KV state diffs.
- Trace payloads: by default we redact fields flagged as PII; I can share a sample OTLP/JSON trace payload.
- SOC2 artifacts: attaching a short pack (redacted) and a pointer to our security portal.
- Private deployment: we support VPC peering (preferred) or site-to-site VPN. For VPN we recommend Palo Alto / Fortinet appliances but peering avoids that complexity. For peering we’ll supply a BGP-less static route flow and CIDR ranges.

Attaching: intersync_test_matrix_v2.xlsx (updated)
Links: https://intersync.io/security/soc2-redacted

Action items we need from RDW:
1) Provide an IdP SAML metadata URL or SCIM endpoint for provisioning test accounts.
2) Confirm IP range we can peer to (or indicate if you prefer VPN).
3) Approve the proposed node-restart window in the runbook (we suggest 30 minutes into the 2nd day of load).

Priya will follow up on infra access.

Best,
Alex

Attachments: intersync_test_matrix_v2.xlsx
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Moreno <alex@intersync.io>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2026 17:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intersync technical qualification kickoff — runbook draft & MAP

Alex / Priya —

Appreciate the quick updates and the v2 matrix. We discussed internally and have a short mutual action plan (MAP) and a runbook draft attached. High-level acceptance criteria:
- Functional: p95 latency <= 220ms for small models, p95 <= 650ms for long-sequence (1k tokens) synthetic tests under baseline load.
- Reliability: graceful fallback to lightweight model variant on node failure with <= 2% error rate increase.
- Security: OTLP traces are redacted for PII and accessible in our audit logs.
- Private deploy: proceed with VPC peering (no VPN). We’ll provide CIDR 10.20.32.0/24 for the peer.

Please review the attached runbook and the MAP items. If acceptable we’ll schedule the pilot kickoff for the week of May 24.

Attachments:
- rdw_intersync_runbook_draft.md (Markdown)
- MAP_Redwood-Intersync_May2026.pdf (PDF stub)

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Platform Partnerships, Redwood Inference
